3. The facts of the case leading to this appeal may be summarized as under;
The Respondent is complainant before the trial court, he has filed a private complaint U/s.200 of Code of Criminal Crl.A.No.1323/2023 Procedure alleging the offence committed by the accused punishable U/s.138 of Negotiable Instrument Act (herein after referred as N.I.Act).

According to the complainant, himself and accused are known to each other from last 5 years before filing of the complaint, accused had availed hand loan of Rs.15,00,000/- from the complainant on 10.01.2015 by way of cash by executing an on demand promissory note and a consideration receipt with a promise to repay the said amount within 3 years and in order to discharge his liability he had issued two cheques bearing No.894962 dated 22.03.2019 for a sum of Rs.7,50,000/- and cheque bearing No.894963 dated 22.04.2019 for a sum of Rs.7,50,000/- respectively drawn on Canara Bank,
Vidyaranyapura Branch, Bengaluru in favour of the complainant, upon presentation of the cheque bearing No.894962 dated 22.03.2019 for encashment it was returned unpaid with bankers endorsement dated Crl.A.No.1323/2023 12.06.2019 as funds insufficient, therefore, complainant on 28.06.2019 issued a demand notice to the accused by RPAD, which was duly served on the accused,
despite the same, accused neither paid the cheque amount nor given any reply.
After compliance of the ingredients of Section 138 of N.I.Act complaint is filed.

The trial court took cognizance and after going through the materials found the prima facie case against accused for an offence punishable U/s.138 of Negotiable Instrument Act, registered criminal case and issued summons.

, Hon'ble Apex court pleased to observe that;
'Sufficient cause' in Section 5 must receive a liberal construction so as to advance substantial justice and generally delay in preferring appeals are required to Crl.A.No.1323/2023 be condoned in the interest of justice where no gross negligence or deliberate inaction or lack of bonafides is imputable to the party seeking condonation of the delay.

When substantial justice and technical consideration are pitted against each other, cause of substantial justice deserves to be preferred for the other side cannot claim to have vested right in injustice being done because of a non-deliberate delay.
It must be grasped that, judiciary is respected not on account of its power to legalize injustice on technical grounds but because it is capable of removing injustice and is expected to do so.'

In the light of ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India and under the facts and circumstances of the present case, this court opined that, it is just and proper to condone the delay of 69 days in preferring this criminal appeal to provide an opportunity to prosecute the petition.
Hence this interim application deserves to be allowed.

The accused has not disputed the signature present on the disputed cheque and also admitted that, cheque in question belong to the bank account maintained by him.

Therefore, it is claimed by the complainant that, legal presumptions enshrined U/s.139 Crl.A.No.1323/2023 and 118 of Negotiable Instrument Act could be raised in his favour, which includes the existence of legally enforceable debt or liability.
19. It is worth to note that, the accused has not disputed nor denied the issuance of the subject cheque.
Hence, initial statutory presumption attached to the cheque as per Section 118(a) and 139 of N.I.Act has to be raised in favour of the complainant.

Section 139 of N.I.Act reads as under;
Sec.139. Presumption in favour of holder.--

It shall be presumed, unless the contrary is proved, that the holder of a cheque received the cheque of the nature referred to in section138 for the discharge,
in whole or in part, of any debt or other liability.

In the case on hand, it is clear that, signature on the cheque having been admitted, a presumption shall be raised under Section 139 of the N.I.Act that the cheque was issued in discharge of debt or liability.

The question to be looked into is as to whether any probable defence was raised by the accused.

sentences.text: On going through the cross-examination of PW.1 it can be noticed that, accused by suggesting the complainant that he was forcibly made to issue blank signed cheques in the police station when complainant had been to the police station to lodge complaint against the accused.
By posing this kind of suggestion, as it is rightly pointed out by the trial court, the accused admitted the issuance of cheques from his account for some Crl.A.No.1323/2023 consideration.
Under the circumstances, as discussed above, the statutory presumption u/s 118(A) and 139 of N.I. Act lies in favour of the complainant, as such onus of disproving the same shifts on the accused.
The accused has not attempted to establish under what circumstances he had issued these cheques to the complainant.
It was the say of the accused before the trial court that he being a chit collector of Tripura Chits Pvt.Ltd., during its closure due to heavy loss he was forced to issue such cheques.
However, this fact has not been admitted by the complainant / CW.1 by saying that there were other 2 persons by name Satisha and Shashi who used to come to collect chit amount.
24. In this scenario, this Court has appreciated the evidence placed before the trial court to analyze the grounds raised by the accused person.
Section 106 of the Indian Crl.A.No.1323/2023 Evidence Act casts burden on the person who asserts the fact which is within his special knowledge.
The N.I.Act is special statute entitle the accused to rebut the presumption.
Except taking bare contention, accused person has not placed iota of evidence to show the previous transactions and repayment of the loan amount.
Therefore, this court is hesitant to believe this unsupported defence of the accused.
In this view of the matter, the formal evidence led by the accused is not sufficient to prove his defence.
26. Another defence of the accused during the cross- examination of PW.1 before the trial court was that complainant had no financial capacity to lend him such a huge loan.

However, from the cross-examination of PW.1 it is elicited that complainant had sold his lands for Rs.52,00,000/- and out of the said sale consideration he had lent loan to the accused on 10.01.2015, as such as a matter of security accused had issued the said two cheques in his favour.
Though, the accused had denied that he had not issued any cheques as security and at the same time he had not rebutted the said fact.

Therefore, as it is rightly observed from the trial court that, the accused has failed to Crl.A.No.1323/2023 raise probable defence and also failed to prove the preponderance of probabilities in his favour.

28. The accused has not issued reply to the statutory notice.
The non-issuance of reply is fatal to the defence.

Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has laid down in the decision reported in (2010) 11 SCC 441; Rangappa V/s. Mohan that;
Crl.A.No.1323/2023 "Very fact that the accused had failed to reply to the statutory notice U/s.138 of N.I.Act leads to inference that there was merit in the complainant's version--
Apart from not raising a probable defence, the appellant accused was not able to contest the existence of a legally enforceable debt or liability."
In the light of the above proposition of law, this court has no hesitation to opined that, non-issuance of the reply to the statutory notice, further strengthens the case of the complainant.
29. It is for the accused to rebut the said presumptions through cogent and convincing evidence.
In case the accused successfully rebut the presumptions, then only the reverse onus shifts on the complainant to prove the transaction in question in detail.
As discussed supra, accused neither taken probable defence, nor established the non-existence of legally recoverable debt.
This aspect has Crl.A.No.1323/2023 reiterated by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of P.Rasiya V/s. Abdul Nazer and another in Crl.A.Nos.1233-1235 of 2022 dated 12.08.2022

By the impugned common judgment and order, the High Court has reversed the concurrent findings recorded by both the courts below and has acquitted the accused on the ground that, in the complaint, the complainant has not specifically stated the nature of transactions and the source of fund.
However, the High Court has failed to note the presumption under Section 139 of the N.I.Act.

As per Section 139 of N.I.Act, it ishall be presumed, unless the contrary is proved, that the holder of a cheque received the cheque of the nature referred to in Section 138 for discharge, in whole or in part, of any debt or other liability.

Therefore, once the initial burden is discharged by the complainant that the Crl.A.No.1323/2023 cheque was issued by the accused and the signature and the issuance of the cheque is not disputed by the accused, in that case,

30. From the discussions made supra, it is crystal clear that, complainant has placed convincing,
corroborative oral and documentary evidence to prove the loan transaction of Rs.7,50,000/- and issuance of a cheque for discharge of the said loan amount.
Apart from that, Crl.A.No.1323/2023 complainant has also proved that, on presentation, said cheque was dishonoured for want of sufficient funds in the bank account maintained by the accused.
The service of legal notice is also proved.
The accused has not repaid the amount covered under the cheque till this day.
He has not placed probable defence to dislodge the statutory presumptions raised in favour of the complainant.
Therefore, this court opined that, the complainant has successfully established the guilt of the accused punishable u/s 138 of Negotiable Instrument Act.
The learned trial Judge has considered all these aspects in proper perspective and rightly held that, accused has committed the offence punishable u/s 138 of N.I.Act.
Accordingly, Points No.2 and 3 under consideration are answered in the Affirmative.
31. POINT NO.4:

The complainant has placed cogent material to show compliance of all the ingredients of Section Crl.A.No.1323/2023 138 of Negotiable Instrument Act, which envisages raising of statutory presumptions in favour of the complainant.
The accused is not successful in placing acceptable contentions to rebut the presumptions.
Thus, the complainant has proved the guilt of the accused punishable u/s 138 of Negotiable Instrument Act.

32. The trial court has assigned proper reasons in the impugned judgment of conviction as against the allegations made in the memorandum of appeal and proceeded to pass conviction and imposed sentence of fine amount.
No grounds are made out in the memorandum of appeal to interfere with the Impugned judgment of conviction.

33. So far as quantum of sentence is concerned, trial court has imposed sentence of fine including the interest that would have been fetched, if it is kept in any fixed deposits and directed the accused to pay fine of Crl.A.No.1323/2023 Rs.8,60,000/- (Rupees Eight Lakhs Sixty Thousand Only) to the complainant for dishonour of a cheque.

Out of fine amount of Rs.8,60,000/- (Rupees Eight Lakhs Sixty Thousand Only) Rs.8,50,000/- (Rupees Eight Lakhs Fifty Thousand Only) shall be paid to the complainant by way of compensation and Rs.10,000/-(Rupee Ten Thousand Only) shall be paid to State exchequer.
In default of payment of fine amount, accused shall undergo simple imprisonment for a period of one year.
Fine amount imposed is within the purview of Section 138 of N.I.Act.
Accused failed to establish the fact that, sentence imposed is exhorbitant and excessive.
There is no merit in the appeal.
Order under appeal is sustainable in law.
Hence, interference of this court is not necessary.
Accordingly, point No.4 under consideration is answered in the Negative.

opennyai_summary.arguments:
Therefore, it is strongly canvassed that the appellant was a collector of Tripura Chits Pvt.Ltd., he was collecting the chits money on behalf of it, the complainant / respondent was one of the members and he was doing the chit business with them, after closure of said company owing to severe loss, the complainant was doing chit fund business with Tripura Chits Pvt.Ltd., the said company owed to some extent of amount to complainant / respondent and no action has been taken against the said chit fund, however filed this false case against the appellant.
Thus, by canvassing that the validity of the cheques had lapsed at the time of filing private Crl.A.No.1323/2023 complaint.
The financial capacity of the complainant to lend huge amount is disputed.
The complainant failed to discharge the burden of proving source of income.
The judgment of the trial court is not maintainable in the eye of law or on facts and accused deserves acquittal.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The onus of proof to rebut this presumption lies on the accused.
The standard of rebuttal evidence depends on the facts and circumstances of each case.
The mere explanation is not enough to rebut this presumption of law, as reported in AIR 2001 SC 3897; Hiten P:. Dalal V/s. Bratinderanath Banerjee and (2006) 6 SCC 39;
M.S.Narayan Menon alias Mani V/s.State of Kerala and another and ILR 2009 KAR 1633; Kumar Exports V/s. Sharma Carpets.
18.
Hence, initial statutory presumption attached to the cheque as per Section 118(a) and 139 of N.I.Act has to be raised in favour of the complainant.
It shall be presumed, unless the contrary is proved, that the holder of a cheque received the cheque of the nature referred to in section138 for the discharge,
in whole or in part, of any debt or other liability.
In the case on hand, it is clear that, signature on the cheque having been admitted, a presumption shall be raised under Section 139 of the N.I.Act that the cheque was issued in discharge of debt or liability.
Section 106 of the Indian Crl.A.No.1323/2023 Evidence Act casts burden on the person who asserts the fact which is within his special knowledge.
The N.I.Act is special statute entitle the accused to rebut the presumption.
Except taking bare contention, accused person has not placed iota of evidence to show the previous transactions and repayment of the loan amount.
On the contrary, it is the specific case of the complainant that the said cheques have been issued as security towards the discharge of loan amount availed by the accused.
No cogent evidence is placed in support of this contention of the accused.
28. The accused has not issued reply to the statutory notice.
The non-issuance of reply is fatal to the defence.
29. It is for the accused to rebut the said presumptions through cogent and convincing evidence.
In case the accused successfully rebut the presumptions, then only the reverse onus shifts on the complainant to prove the transaction in question in detail.
As discussed supra, accused neither taken probable defence, nor established the non-existence of legally recoverable debt.
Accused failed to establish the fact that, sentence imposed is exhorbitant and excessive.
opennyai_summary.decision:
32. The trial court has assigned proper reasons in the impugned judgment of conviction as against the allegations made in the memorandum of appeal and proceeded to pass conviction and imposed sentence of fine amount.
33. So far as quantum of sentence is concerned, trial court has imposed sentence of fine including the interest that would have been fetched, if it is kept in any fixed deposits and directed the accused to pay fine of Crl.A.No.1323/2023 Rs.8,60,000/- (Rupees Eight Lakhs Sixty Thousand Only) to the complainant for dishonour of a cheque.
Out of fine amount of Rs.8,60,000/- (Rupees Eight Lakhs Sixty Thousand Only) Rs.8,50,000/- (Rupees Eight Lakhs Fifty Thousand Only) shall be paid to the complainant by way of compensation and Rs.10,000/-(Rupee Ten Thousand Only) shall be paid to State exchequer.
In default of payment of fine amount, accused shall undergo simple imprisonment for a period of one year.
Fine amount imposed is within the purview of Section 138 of N.I.Act.
Order under appeal is sustainable in law.
Accordingly, point No.4 under consideration is answered in the Negative.
POINT NO.5:-
In view of findings on the above points No.1 to 4, this criminal appeal is devoid of merits and the same is liable to be dismissed by confirming impugned judgment of conviction and order of sentence.
Hence, this court proceed to pass the following:
ORDER This Criminal Appeal u/s 374(3) of Code of Criminal Procedure filed by the appellant is dismissed.
Consequently, the judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 06.06.2023 passed in C.C.No.16641/2019 on the file of XX Addl.Chief Metropolitan Magistrate,
Bengaluru is confirmed.
Appellant is directed to appear before the Trial Court to deposit the fine amount or to serve the default sentence.
